Commentary.Commentary: So 196 is what Ireland need to win this game and take a 1-0 lead in this series. They are still in pole position in this game and would look to achieve this target. Netherlands have given themselves something to bowl at. The pitch has not looked easy to bat and the hosts will feel they are in with a decent shout. Can the bowlers exploit the conditions or will Ireland scale this mountain? Join us for the chase to find out.

A decent bowling effort from Ireland but they will be disappointed to have let away runs towards the end and will also be unhappy not to have bowled out Netherlands earlier. Josh Little and Craig Young were the stars with the ball. Little's pace wrecked havoc as the left arm  seamer finished with 3/32. Craig Young was also impressive as he too finished with a 3-fer. Spinners Simi Singh and Andy McBrine were impressive as well as they gave away just 59 runs in their 19 overs with both getting one wicket apiece. George Dockrell and Barry McCarthy were the only bowlers to go wicketless and be expensive.

Winning the toss and opting to bat, Netherlands started off solidly as they found themselves at 51/1 but the wicket of Max O'Dowd turned the tide as they found themselves reeling at 53/5. Bas de Leede and Saqib Zulfiqar steadied the ship with a 49-run stand. The duo departed in quick succession and it looked like the innings would be wrapped up quickly. Timm van der Gugten though had other ideas. He took the attack to the Irish bowlers. When 150 looked farfetched his 49 along with a supportive 29 from Logan van Beek has taken them close to 200!

A decent bowling effort from Ireladn but they will rue the fact they could not finish things off with the ball as they would have liked and let Netherlands get past 150. Netherlands will be the side entering the break with momentum and bigger smiles on their face. Thanks to Timm van der Gugten they have a very respectable target to bowl at.

Who will bowl from the other end with the other new ball? It will be Craig Young!
A decent start then for Netherlands. 4 from the first! Good length and on middle, this is pushed to mid on.
Sligjt misfield and another single. Length again and on off, SM guides it to point. The fielder does not stop it cleanly and it is an easy run.
Max is up and running! Nice, confident push! Length and around off, slightly fuller, this is pushed through covers for one.
Myburgh is off the mark! On the pads, this is nudged around the corner for one.
Lovely! Got the last one to come back in and gets this one to shape away. The length is also nice and full, enticing the batter to drive. Stephan does so loosely and he is beaten.
Some shape into the batter! The length is a touch shorter. The line is a little too straight. Myburgh looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. High on the pads.
WIDE! Netherlands are underway courtesy an extra! Down the leg side by Barry. It is left alone. Wided.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Ireland players make their way out on the field as they scatter to take their respective positions. Max O'Dowd and Stephan Myburgh stride out to open the innings for the Netherlands. Barry McCarthy is all set to operate with the new ball.

Ireland skipper, Andy Balbirnie  says that they would have batted too and feels the pitch will break up later. Tells they are targetting 30 points in every series. Admits they were not at their best against Afghanistan in UAE. Tells he is feeling good and tells the boys are in a good place. Andy tells Stirling has been in great touch. Adds Little has been good with the ball.

Pieter Seelaar says the wicket looks pretty nice and he feels the wicket will get lower and slower as the day goes on. States it has been rainy but the sun is out, they played a couple of ODIs and they are in good shape. Adds they are very excited and are looking forward for this game. Ends by saying, they are raring to go and are all fired up.

PITCH REPORT - Peter Borren and Niall O'Brien are the pitch masters for the day. Borren says that the pitch looks dry and the weather has not been great. Tells the pitch has decent grass coverage and tells that the pitch looks hard. O'Brien says that it should be a cracking game.

Netherlands Playing XI - Max O'Dowd, Stephan Myburgh, Ben Cooper, Pieter Seelaar (C), Bas de Leede, Scott Edwards (WK), Logan van Beek, Timm van der Gugten, Vivian Kingma, Brandon Glover, Fred Klaassen.
Ireland Playing XI - Paul Stirling, William Porterfield, Andrew Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Simi Singh, George Dockrell, Craig Young, Andy McBrine, Joshua Little, Barry McCarthy.
TOSS - The coin falls in favour of Pieter Seelaar. NETHERLANDS OPT TO BAT!

Hello and welcome to the first of the three match ODI series between Ireland and Netherlands. Despite it being familiar conditions for the latter, it is the visitors who are the favourites heading into it. They have most of their big names and are a stronger side on paper. The home side have a few big players missing but this gives the others a chance to prove their mettle. Also, the Netherlands will be starting their campaign in the Super League so they will want to start off with a win. Can they do so? We will find out.
